Ukraine Sees Exponential Growth in Private Security Firms Providing Anti-Drone Protection — In November last year Ukraine’s Defense Ministry unveiled a project to allow private businesses to defend their own plants against Russian aerial attacks. Now more than 50 enterprises have obtained permits to use licensed security firms or their own trained staff to supplement the country’s national air-defense network.

Russian Drones Just Miss Former CIA Director David Petraeus: a View From a Train Near the Polish Border — Kyiv Post presents an eyewitness account of the attack on a train at the Polish border that nearly hit former CIA Director David Petraeus and came on the heels of ex-UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s departure.

Ukraine Has Leverage Over Trump Now — Timothy Ash argues that President Trump cannot blame Ukraine alone for rising energy prices, saying his Iran policy and decision to reduce US support for Kyiv helped push Ukraine toward developing its own long-range strike capabilities and gave it greater leverage over Washington.

‘The Battlefield Has Gone Underground’: Khartiia Commander Reveals Ukraine’s Edge Over Russia — The commander of Ukraine’s 2nd Khartiia Corps said the battlefield in his sector has shifted underground, where Ukrainian troops are operating more effectively than Russian forces. He also urged Ukraine and its Western partners to develop short-range missiles against Russia’s jet-powered drones.

Ukraine Must Attack Russia’s Missile Plants to Win War, MITS Capital CEO Says — MITS Capital co-founder and CEO Perry Boyle told Kyiv’s Yalta European Strategy Forum that air defense alone cannot save Ukraine and urged partners to back attacks on Russia’s missile-production plants. He also criticized weak foreign investment in Ukraine’s defense sector. Budget Committee Chair Roksolana Pidlasa echoed his call to focus on defeating Russia.

Russian Attack on Pryluky Kills 3, Wounds 7 — Three people were killed and seven injured when Russian forces attacked an agricultural enterprise in central Pryluky, Chernihiv region. At least two explosions were recorded, damaging windows in nearby apartment buildings, while police warned residents to avoid the area because of the threat of another attack.

Russia Launches Kalibr Cruise Missiles Directly From Base, Ukraine Says — Ukraine’s navy said Russia has been launching the naval-based Kalibr missiles directly from port, instead of sending the warships out at sea, for four months in a row. Russia also reportedly has four vessels capable of launching the missile left in the Black Sea, with cruise missile launches relatively rare in recent months.

Kharkiv Holds First Pride March Since Russia’s Full-Scale Invasion — KharkivPride held its first march on foot since Russia launched its full-scale invasion, with about 200 people following a 500-meter underground route. Participants called for legal recognition of same-sex partnerships, stronger hate-crime legislation, and greater attention to equality and civilian safety.

Germany Plans €3.4B Tomahawk Missile Purchase — Germany’s Defense Ministry plans to earmark nearly €3.4 billion for US-made Tomahawk cruise missiles and mobile Typhon launchers, POLITICO reported. The acquisition would give the Bundeswehr its first ground-based long-range strike capability, though the amount may change and the purchase still requires budgetary and parliamentary approval.

Ukraine May Get License for Older, Less Advanced Patriot Missiles — US President Donald Trump said Washington is discussing a license to allow Ukraine to manufacture a less advanced version of its Patriot interceptor missiles. The proposal appears to revive a plan Trump announced in July but later questioned on grounds of “security.” US officials also warned that setting up production would take years and would not ease Kyiv’s immediate air-defense shortages.

Canada Considers Joining EU €90 Billion Ukraine Loan — Canada is negotiating participation in the European Union’s €90 billion loan for Ukraine, which will finance Kyiv’s budgetary and defense needs in 2026 and 2027. The talks come as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks closer ties with Europe and aims to reduce Canada’s dependence on the United States.

Ukraine’s EU Membership Path Faces New Risk as Outgoing Prosecutor General Targets NABU — Ruslan Kravchenko’s resignation and subsequent announcement of a case against NABU’s director have renewed scrutiny of Ukraine’s EU reform commitments. Judicial reform advocate Mykhailo Zhernakov says the next prosecutor general’s selection must involve international experts, while parliament must restore safeguards in judicial appointments.

Exclusive: Poland’s FM Radek Sikorski Comments for Kyiv Post — Poland’s FM said Russia’s new jet-powered drones pose a threat that requires action from both Ukraine and its allies. Speaking at the YES Conference in Kyiv, he also praised Ukraine’s resilience and reaffirmed Poland’s solidarity with Kyiv.

Ukraine’s Prosecutor General Leaves Country Amid Anti-Corruption Showdown — Ukraine’s Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko reportedly left the country overnight in an official vehicle, amid an escalating clash with anti-corruption agencies and now involving President Volodymyr Zelensky. His departure came hours after he accused NABU chief Semen Kryvonos of crimes, prompting the president to call for the chief prosecutor’s dismissal.

Why ‘Sanctioning Russia Act’ Is Putin’s Biggest Nightmare — If the US House of Representatives passes the “Sanctioning Russia Act,” which mandates a 100% maximum tariff on the five largest countries buying Russian oil and gas and punishes countries helping Russia evade sanctions, it could be game over for the Russian economy.

Polish FM: ‘We Would Defeat Russia Quite Quickly’ if Moscow Attacked NATO — Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said NATO has “overwhelming superiority” in air power and could defeat Russia “quite quickly” if Moscow attacked, adding that Europe could destroy Russia’s remaining refining capacity in weeks.

Ukraine Faces New Russian Jet-Powered Drones | Stefan Korshak — Ukraine Brief on TVP World is joined by Stefan Korshak, Senior Defense Correspondent at the Kyiv Post, to discuss the escalating attacks and Ukraine’s air-defense challenges. While Ukraine can intercept many conventional drones and ballistic missiles, faster jet-powered Geran drones are creating increasingly difficult threats.

So You Want to Be a MilTech Millionaire? — Ukraine is rapidly becoming a major player in military techology. Now foreign defense manufacturers are flooding into the country to take advantage of the opportunity to test and develop products in actual battle conditions. Here are some of the pitfalls to be aware of on both sides.

Poland Scrambles Security Chiefs After Russian Strike Near Border With Ukraine — Poland’s prime minister convened an emergency security meeting after a Russian strike hit a Kyiv-Warsaw train near the Ukrainian border, as Donald Tusk warned Moscow’s escalating actions could eventually threaten Polish territory.

Trump Tells Zelensky to Stop ‘Knocking Out Diesel Fuel in Russia’ — Trump urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to stop striking diesel fuel facilities in Russia, warning that other targets should be pursued instead. Ukraine’s attacks on Russian energy infrastructure have disrupted fuel production and contributed to domestic shortages. Trump says peace efforts are progressing, but Poland’s foreign minister remains skeptical as Russia maintains its war objectives.

Why Boris Johnson? Putin’s Long-Running Grudge in Focus After Train Strike — A near-miss Russian drone strike at Yahodyn station has cast fresh light on Vladimir Putin’s long-running hostility toward Boris Johnson. The former British prime minister has stood near the top of the Kremlin’s list of Western adversaries because of his early and outspoken support for Ukraine’s defense.

Russian Drone Strike Narrowly Misses Boris Johnson, Carl Bildt and Ex-CIA Chief David Petraeus — Ukraine and Poland say the Russian drone strike near the border may have been aimed at the diplomatic train carrying Boris Johnson and other senior Western officials, which had passed through Yahodyn shortly before the attack.

Amid Air Raid Sirens and Shelter Shows, Ukrainian Fashion Week ‘Unbreakable’ — In Kyiv, Ukrainian Fashion Week's Spring/Summer 2027 season pressed on through a week of daytime Russian strikes, moving three runway shows into a bomb shelter. Designers and organizers called Russian attacks the most disruptive yet, but the season closed on a high, with designer Oleksandra Sakhaudinova winning the Grand Prix for "Reclaiming the Light."

Russian Hackers Used Claude AI to Target Ukraine — Threat groups linked to Russian intelligence services used Anthropic’s Claude AI tool to execute multi-victim cyber campaigns targeting Ukrainian and Western institutions, according to a threat intelligence report by Anthropic. The US company stated it disrupted operations over the past six months, identifying the Russian SVR-linked group Midnight Blizzard and an operator using the moniker “JackPoterz.” Intrusions targeted Ukrainian government m

A Visit to a Unique Porcelain Museum in Kyiv — The Kyiv Porcelain Museum is a unique institution that continues to operate despite the war. It showcases numerous rare and highly valuable porcelain pieces from a variety of manufacturers while introducing visitors to the history and artistry of porcelain. The museum is headed by our colleague, Oleksandr Shvets, who is also its founder and owner.

Keeping the Bridges Open — Moscow’s attacks are turning the Dnipro river into a daily barrier between the city’s two halves. But there are fears not only for Kyiv’s physical bridges, with the need to also maintain social bonds across Ukraine, especially as winter approaches and hopes for peace recede.

Meloni Rules Out Alliances With Opponents of Ukraine Aid — Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni rejected speculation that she could form political coalitions with parties opposed to military aid for Ukraine, saying that she will not abandon her principles for electoral advantage ahead of elections next year. Her comments deliver a sharp warning to far-right politician Roberto Vannacci, an outspoken critic of arms deliveries to Kyiv who has gained momentum in domestic polls.

Germany Weighs Restricting NATO Defense Plans if AfD Governs — German defense officials are considering steps to block regional state governments from accessing confidential national and NATO defense plans if the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) enters government. Following state elections in Saxony-Anhalt where the AfD won 44% of the vote and 39 of 83 seats, Defense Minister Boris Pistorius moved to ensure that a state government led by the pro-Russian party cannot compromise sensitive o

Italian Ex-Foreign Minister Giulio Terzi: Italy Is Unequivocally on Ukraine’s Side — There can be no doubt that Feb. 24, 2022 was a watershed. Since then, security, deterrence and defense against the tangible threat of extremely serious military aggression have once again become central concerns.

Sikorski Urges Aggressive NATO Drills Near Kaliningrad — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski argued that NATO should conduct aggressive military exercises near Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave to exploit Moscow’s localized vulnerabilities and force Vladimir Putin to redeploy troops away from Ukraine. Sikorski noted that Kaliningrad currently holds “practically no troops” because the Kremlin assumes NATO will not act, suggesting decisive allied maneuvers would inject strategic ambiguity.

Russia’s ‘Beacon’ for Sick Children, Facing Jail for Pro-Peace Message — Prominent Russian charity leader and children’s hospice founder Lida Moniava has been placed under supervised curfew and fitted with an ankle monitor pending trial on charges of spreading “false information” about the Russian army. The charges against the 38-year-old founder of the “House with the Lighthouse” foundation stem from a 2023 Telegram post citing UN civilian casualty statistics and calling for aid to Ukrainian re

Putin’s Economic Growth Claims Diverge From IMF Data — Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed at the BRICS summit in New Delhi that Russia’s economy expanded 10.3% from 2023 to 2025, outpacing global benchmarks despite 30,000 sanctions, while alleging an 8% drop in EU industrial output. IMF data shows global economic growth reached 10.7% over the same timeframe, while Eurostat records an EU industrial decline of just 0.6%.

Russian Strike in Kramatorsk Kills 2, Wounds 4 — A Russian strike targeted a civilian car moving through the center of Kramatorsk in Donetsk region on Sunday morning, Sept. 13, killing two people and injuring four others, according to Donetsk Regional Military Administration Head Vadym Filashkin. Emergency services deployed to the scene as authorities worked to determine the full extent of the damage. Filashkin condemned the deliberate assault on civilians and renewed urgent appeals for resident

Sweden Votes in Election Thriller, far Right Eyes Govt Role — Sweden began voting on Sunday, Sept. 13, in a closely contested general election that will determine whether the far-right enters government for the first time or the left-wing opposition reclaims power. Opposition leader Magdalena Andersson of the Social Democrats warned against a cabinet dominated by the Sweden Democrats, while conservative Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson campaigned on law-and-order gains, pledging ministerial posts

Territory Remains Main Obstacle to Ukraine-Russia Deal, Kushner Says — US special envoy Jared Kushner stated at the YES 2026 conference in Kyiv that territorial disputes remain the chief obstacle preventing a peace agreement between Ukraine and Russia. Kushner explained that while Vladimir Putin outlined Moscow’s territorial demands, Ukraine firmly refuses to retreat, leaving mediators to craft a creative formula that satisfies Kyiv while compelling Russia to end hostilities. Kushner noted that

China Threatens to Cancel US Summit Over Taiwan Arms — China warned the US that it intends to cancel a planned leaders’ summit this month if Washington approves new arms transfers to Taiwan beforehand, Kyodo reported. Beijing reiterated that the status of Taiwan remains an inviolable “red line,” following heightened friction after Donald Trump previously described arms sales as a “bargaining chip”.

Russia Faces Shortage of Chinese Drone Jet Engines — Russian forces are facing disruptions in supplies of Chinese-manufactured jet engines for long-range strike drones due to coordinated measures by Ukraine and international partners, HUR Deputy Head Vadym Skibitsky said. Skibitsky noted that while Ukrainian intelligence has identified all Russian manufacturing enterprises and joint ventures with Chinese firms, striking them is complicated because they are located over 2,000 kilometers from the

Peace Through Strength NOW! — Over 700 leaders, diplomats, and veterans from 28 countries convened in Kyiv for the 22nd Annual Meeting of the Yalta European Strategy (YES), held Sept. 11-12 under the motto “Peace Through Strength NOW!” Organized by the Victor Pinchuk Foundation, the forum focused on accelerating military aid, expanding defense manufacturing, and reinforcing air defense ahead of winter.

Russia Fired 2,100 Drones and 78 Missiles This Week, Zelensky Says — Russian forces launched approximately 2,100 strike drones, 78 missiles, and 1,700 guided aerial bombs against Ukraine over the past week, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Sept. 13. Zelensky highlighted that a substantial share consisted of jet-powered Shahed drones designed to batter Ukraine’s economy and life-support networks, citing Sunday strikes on energy, railway, and residential infrastructure across Odes

Hard Times Ahead: Russian Attacks put Ukraine’s Finances Under Pressure — Senior economic and financial officials warned at the YES 2026 conference in Kyiv that Ukraine’s state budget faces a “very difficult winter” driven by escalating war costs and systematic Russian strikes on commercial, logistics, and port infrastructure. Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko estimated annual damage to infrastructure and fixed assets at roughly $10 billion, warning state compensation tools cannot meet busin

UN Warns Ukraine Faces Toughest Wartime Winter Yet — United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Administrator Alexander De Croo warned in an interview with the BBC that Ukraine could face its most difficult winter since the 2022 invasion due to systematic Russian strikes on civilian and energy infrastructure. De Croo noted that Ukraine enters the heating season from a very weak position, with severe damage to transmission lines, fuel stations, and urban centers raising the risk of widespread he

‘A Way for Russian Occupiers Go Home’: Ukraine Intel Reveals Why Kerch Bridge Still Stands — Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence says the Kerch Bridge remains politically symbolic but has lost much of its military value as Russia relies more on land routes through occupied southern Ukraine. Deputy intelligence chief Vadym Skibitsky says Kyiv is now focused on disrupting wider logistics networks, countering Russia’s missile and drone production, and using strikes and sanctions to pressure the supply c

Drones Target Nizhnekamsk Hub and Slavyansk Refinery in Russia — Unmanned aerial vehicles struck key Russian petroleum and chemical production hubs early Sunday morning, Sept. 13, targeting the industrial cluster in Nizhnekamsk, Republic of Tatarstan, and igniting a fire at an oil refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban, Krasnodar Krai. Nizhnekamsk houses some of Russia’s largest refining and petrochemical enterprises, including Tatneft’s TANECO refinery, TAIF-NK, and synthetic rubber producer Nizhnekams

Russian Strikes Hit Gas Station, Kyiv-Warsaw Train, Near Polish Border — Russian forces struck near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk checkpoint on the Ukrainian-Polish border on Sunday morning, Sept. 13, damaging a gas station, igniting several trucks, and striking the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train two kilometers from the border. Preemptive warnings prevented train casualties, and border operations resumed after temporary sheltering. Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha condemned the assault as Vlad

Budanov Eyes Trilateral Ukraine Peace Talks in October — Head of the Office of the President Kyrylo Budanov announced at the YES 2026 conference in Kyiv that a renewed round of trilateral peace negotiations could take place in early October, focusing on practical measures to curb aerial strikes against critical infrastructure and ensure safe navigation in the Black Sea. Following consultations with national security advisers from the UK, France, Germany, and Italy, Budanov emphasized that direct

Russian Strikes Injure 23 Across Odesa, Ternopil, and Konotop — Russian forces launched widespread missile and drone strikes across Ukraine on Sunday morning, Sept. 13, injuring at least 23 people. In Odesa, continuous attacks damaged a residential high-rise, private homes, the Botanical Garden, warehouses, and a children’s sanatorium, injuring nine. In western Ukraine, drone strikes hit a transport facility and industrial building in Ternopil, injuring one, while an attack on Konotop in Sumy re

9/11: Geopolitical Legacy 25 Years On — Marking the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, European newspapers evaluated the long-term consequences for global security, international law, and Western democratic cohesion. While the attacks initially unified Western democracies, subsequent US military campaigns in Afghanistan and Iraq accelerated institutional overreach, entrenched permanent surveillance practices, and fostered deep political polarization.

Ukraine Tests Automated Drone Warning System for Gas Stations — Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced that Ukraine is testing an automated early warning system to alert filling station networks of approaching drones following intensified Russian strikes. The software predicts drone trajectories to trigger preemptive safety measures, with plans to expand the platform to other industrial sectors. The government also agreed to reinforce physical blast barriers at stations, fast-track customs fo

Putin Rejects Zelensky’s Proposal for Miami G20 Talks — Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected President Volodymyr Zelensky’s proposal to hold direct talks on ending the war at the G20 summit in Miami, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said. Peskov described a Florida meeting as “impossible,” stating Putin is willing to meet Zelensky exclusively in Moscow. Zelensky had stated that he was prepared to attend the Dec. 14-15 summit in Miami if Putin attended, stressing the need for concrete diploma

Ukraine Is Better Prepared for Winter Strikes, Koretskyi Says — Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi announced at the YES 2026 conference in Kyiv that Ukraine is significantly better prepared for Russian attacks on its power grid than last winter, though fully protecting every facility remains impossible. Koretskyi noted that the government has developed multi-tiered contingency plans focused on decentralized energy and utility systems.

Russian Strikes Hit Odesa High-Rise, Postal Depot, and Power Grid — Russian forces struck southern Ukraine overnight Saturday-Sunday, hitting a residential high-rise in Odesa and striking a Nova Poshta logistics branch with a jet-powered drone, injuring two people. Concurrently, a Russian strike on energy infrastructure in Mykolaiv caused localized blackouts across several city districts.

Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Russian Attack Halts US-Owned Oleina Sunflower Oil Plant in Dnipro — A Sept. 10 Russian attack damaged part of the US agribusiness giant Bunge’s production in Dnipro, forcing the facility to suspend operations. This was the second major Russian strike on the plant of 2026. While Bunge confirmed no plant staff were injured, local authorities reported two overall fatalities in Dnipro and damage to 14 vehicles near the facility.

Russian Court Disqualifies Liberal Yabloko Party List in Tomsk — A court in western Siberia’s Tomsk region disqualified the liberal Yabloko party’s candidate list ahead of upcoming regional elections, upholding a lawsuit filed by the LDPR. The ruling leaves the northwestern Novgorod region as the only Russian territory where Yabloko candidates remain eligible to run, as regional authorities have now blocked or denied list registration across seven regions.

When Statecraft Becomes Transaction — US President Trump and his special envoys appear unable to break out of the businessman’s transactional mindset. But in geopolitics there are too many unquantifiable factors to consider, which inevitably sabotage any “dealmaking” approach based on assets and liabilities.

Leipzig Drone Attack Explosives Disguised in Food Can, Probe Finds — An attempted drone attack on a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at Germany’s Leipzig/Halle Airport on Aug. 4 failed only because a detonator wire snapped, leaving 1.8 kilograms of Semtex concealed inside a vegetable tin can unexploded, Welt am Sonntag reported. German investigators identified two primary suspects linked to Russian military intelligence (GRU) – Belarusian national Andrei K. and Russian national Oleg L. – who smu

EU Eastern Border Irregular Crossings Drop 47% — Irregular crossings along the EU’s Eastern Land Border route dropped 47% in the first eight months of 2026, with Frontex recording just over 4,000 detections. The decline coincides with extensive border fortifications across Poland, the Baltic states, and Finland, including Poland’s €2.3 billion East Shield project. Total irregular entries across the EU decreased by 35% to roughly 75,000, with declines recorded across nearly all major corridors ex

Russian Strikes Hit Railway Facilities in Fastiv and Lutsk — Russian forces struck railway infrastructure in Fastiv, Kyiv region, and Lutsk on Saturday, Sept. 12, according to Ukrzaliznytsia Board Chairman Oleksandr Pertsovskyi. Preemptive evacuation protocols ensured no passengers or staff were injured. Concurrently, the rail operator temporarily truncated direct train service to Sumy, terminating routes at Konotop and replacing the final leg with bus shuttles due to intensified attacks on roll

Russian Military Slang Reveals the Reality of Life on the Front Line — A 250-page study of almost 7,000 communications between Russian military personnel and their relatives in 2025 illustrated the reality of life in the combat zone for those fed into the “meat grinder” that is Putin’s “special military operation.”

Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Command Posts and Supply Depots — Ukrainian forces struck multiple Russian military command posts, drone storage sites, and equipment depots on Sept. 11 and early Sept. 12. Precision strikes hit UAV command posts in Polohy and Zaliznyi Port, as well as drone warehouses in Donetsk, Selydove, Kurakhivka, and Malyi Kermenchyk. In occupied Alchevsk, forces targeted a logistics warehouse and weapons depot.

Ukraine Hits Russian Chemical Plants and Taganrog Drone Sites, Zelensky Says — Ukrainian forces struck two chemical industry enterprises in Russia’s Perm and Samara regions and a Black Sea target over the past 24 hours. Concurrently, the SBU reported that its “Alpha” special operations units hit an FPV drone production plant, two drone warehouses, a Pantsir-S2 air defense system, an oil tank, and a P-18 radar in Taganrog, sparking fires across the facilities.

Russia’s War in Ukraine Has Cost Poland’s Economy More than €100 bln, Estimate Shows — Russia’s full-scale war in Ukraine cost Poland an estimated €113.4 billion between 2022 and 2025, according to Statistics Poland. The losses include reduced economic output, higher inflation, lower real wage growth, and increased defense and Ukraine-related spending.

AFU Gains Ground, Kuban Gets Pounded, NATO Trains Hard and Gives Russian Drone Free Pass — A roundup of the weeks biggest military and political events in Ukraine. The AFU finally announces the results of its somewhat secret Lyman counteroffensive. Ukraine is poised to defeat Russia’s Black Sea Fleet – again. The air battle continues with tit-for-tat barrages. And the Kushner-Witkoff vaudeville show bombs.

Modi Urges Putin to End War in Ukraine at BRICS Talks — Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring an end to the war against Ukraine during bilateral talks on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi. Emphasizing that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only pathway to resolution, Modi and Putin also addressed maritime security challenges in the Black Sea, where recent strikes on merchant shipping resulted in the deaths of at least five Indian sailors

EU Examines Funding for Ukraine-Led FREYJA Missile Defense System — The European Commission is considering financial support for FREYJA, a pan-European anti-ballistic missile project initiated by Ukraine, EU Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said on Friday, Sept. 11. Funding could be drawn from the €90 billion Ukraine support loan or the €1.5 billion EDIP mechanism amid acute shortages of US-made interceptors.

Ukraine Revises Q2 GDP Growth Down to 0.4%, Below NBU Estimate — Ukraine’s State Statistics Service revised its second-quarter 2026 GDP estimate down to 0.4% year-on-year, from a 0.6% flash estimate, and to 0.3% quarter-on-quarter, below the National Bank’s earlier 0.8% calculation. Nominal GDP reached just under Hr. 2.31 trillion ($51.8 billion).

Russian Ballistic Missiles Strike Zaporizhstal Steel Plant, Injuring 4 — Russian forces struck the Zaporizhstal metallurgical plant in Zaporizhzhia with four ballistic missiles early Saturday morning, Sept. 12, injuring four workers and inflicting critical damage on blast furnace equipment and power infrastructure. The attack marks the third missile attack on the Metinvest-owned plant in a month, with production remaining halted since late August strikes.

Ukraine Sets Sept. 20 Deadline for Simplified AWOL Return — Ukraine’s simplified return program for servicemen who went absent without official leave (AWOL) is set to conclude on Sept. 20, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine announced. During August 2026, the number of soldiers voluntarily returning to service exceeded new unauthorized departures. The initiative permits servicemen who left units on or before June 12 to select their preferred military branch, unit, and position, whil

Drone Debris, Live Warheads Discovered in Romania and Black Sea — The Romanian Ministry of National Defence reported the discovery and neutralization of debris from multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) on Friday, Sept. 11, across Tulcea County, the Black Sea, and areas north of Constanța. Military EOD teams safely neutralized an active warhead found in Black Sea waters and an interceptor drone containing an unexploded charge.

How will Sweden Vote on 13 September? — Sweden’s centre-left opposition and governing centre-right coalition have both been hit by political controversies on the eve of Sunday’s parliamentary election. While the center-left opposition maintains a narrow lead in polls, the Left Party faces internal friction after removing candidates over allegations of antisemitism and support for terrorism. Concurrently, the governing bloc faces controversy after reports revealed that an official of the right-wi

Zelensky Ready to Meet Putin at Miami G20 if Russian Leader Attends — President Volodymyr Zelensky said that he is ready to travel to Miami for the G20 summit in December to hold direct talks with Vladimir Putin if the Russian leader attends. Zelensky stressed that the focus must be on achieving concrete results rather than exchanging rhetoric.

Russia’s Deployed Nuclear Warheads Hit Post-2017 High — Russia has increased its number of deployed nuclear warheads for the fourth consecutive year, reaching 1,796 operational warheads as of January 2026 – the highest level since 2017, according to SIPRI’s annual World Nuclear Forces report. Russia’s total stockpile stands at 5,420 warheads, with 2,604 in storage and 1,020 retired. Ground-based ICBMs account for roughly 892 deployed warheads, while strategic bombers were dispersed to remote air

Most Ukrainian Refugees in Poland Plan to Return Home, Survey Finds — A survey by the Rating Group found that 51% of Ukrainian refugees in Poland plan to return to Ukraine, though 43% of these respondents plan to wait until after the war ends and only 8% plan an imminent return. Security and stability remain the primary condition for 71% of respondents. Meanwhile, 44% expressed a preference to stay abroad permanently.

Medvedev Dismisses Rumors of Imminent Russian Mobilization — Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev dismissed assertions that Moscow is preparing a new military mobilization, calling the reports lies and provocations ahead of State Duma elections. Medvedev claimed Russia has no need for a draft, asserting that claims of an impending call-up are intended to rattle the domestic population.

Russia Is Hunting Civilians in Kramatorsk — FPV drones, glide bombs and strikes on marked humanitarian vehicles are emptying a city – and that is the point. Unable to conquer Ukrainian cities and land through sheer military force, Russia resorts to dehumanizing the places and turning them into wastelands.

Russian Missile and Drone Barrage Hits Odesa Region, Injuring 35 — Russian forces launched a massive missile and drone assault targeting the Odesa region early Saturday morning, Sept. 12, injuring at least 35 people in the regional capital and five others – including four children – in Chornomorsk. A residential fire engulfed multiple upper floors of a 25-story apartment building, while strikes damaged gas lines, private homes, and a rehabilitation facility.

US House to Vote Next Week on Graham’s Russia Sanctions Bill — The US House of Representatives will vote next week on a bipartisan Russia sanctions bill championed by Senator Lindsey Graham. Considered under simple-majority rules, the legislation authorizes US President Donald Trump to impose 100% tariffs on the five largest purchasers of Russian crude oil and natural gas, as well as on five nations facilitating sanctions evasion

Drones Strike Taganrog Airfield and Tolyatti Chemical Plant — Drone strikes early Saturday morning, Sept. 12, hit both the Taganrog-Tsentralny military airfield in Russia’s Rostov region and the KuibyshevAzot chemical plant in Tolyatti, Samara region. Detonations and thick smoke were recorded across the base housing Russia’s 708th Military Transport Aviation Regiment and the 325th Aircraft Repair Plant in Taganrog. In Tolyatti, drones sparked a major blaze at KuibyshevAzot, a vital defense suppl

Zelensky Warns of Reciprocal Strikes if Russia Targets Power Grid — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Ukraine will strike back symmetrically if Russia attacks its power grid this winter, pledging to respond in kind if Moscow induces blackouts. Speaking to Fareed Zakaria and at the Yalta European Strategy summit on Friday, Sept. 11, Zelensky advocated for a mutual “energy truce” to protect energy infrastructure on both sides alongside unblocking the Black Sea food corridor.

Russian Strikes Kill 3, Injure 5 in Kryvyi Rih and Kharkiv — Russian forces launched ballistic missiles and attack drones against Kryvyi Rih overnight Friday-Saturday, killing two people, leaving one missing, and injuring three, while damaging an industrial enterprise, five apartment buildings, a healthcare center, and three schools. The barrage followed a Friday evening drone strike on Kharkiv’s Kyivskyi district that killed a 32-year-old man and injured two others

Russian Missile-Drone Attack Hits Odesa Apartment Building, Injures Six — A Russian missile and drone attack damaged a residential high-rise in Odesa early Saturday, injuring at least six people, all of whom were hospitalized.

Russian Official to Attend G20 Energy Talks in Houston Despite Previous EU Protests — A Russian official will attend G20 energy talks in Houston weeks after Moscow’s return to an in-person G20 meeting drew protests from European officials over the war in Ukraine.

Putin Admits Russia Is World’s Biggest Sanctions Target, Ramps Up Anti-West Rhetoric — In a BRICS speech and Q&A with Russian journalists, Putin attacked the G7, NATO and European leaders while portraying BRICS as a rising alternative to Western influence.

Putin Threatens Europe Over Possible Troop Deployment in Ukraine — Russian President Vladimir Putin issued another threat to Europe, warning that deploying troops to Ukraine would mean war with Russia, while simultaneously claiming Moscow poses no threat to the continent.
Russian Drone Strikes Zaporizhzhia Home, Killing Woman — A Russian drone destroyed a private home in Zaporizhzhia, killing a woman as Moscow continued aerial attacks across Ukrainian cities.
